newsitem.title: USA: Dlr ends mixed in U.S. as mark/yen surge continues.
newsitem.headline: Dlr ends mixed in U.S. as mark/yen surge continues.

text.p: The dollar closed lower against the mark, but edged higher against the yen, trading in tandem with the continuing rally in mark/yen, dealers said.

Confirmation of the Bundesbank's apparent determination to hold German interest rates steady bolstered the German unit across the board, especially against the yen, which suffers from puny Japanese investment returns, dealers said.
The mark also benefited from continued profit-taking after the recent demise of a sterling/mark and dollar/mark rally, dealers said.

The Bundesbank council at its regular meeting Thursday voted not to move rates, affirming public comments one day earlier from Bundesbank officials saying they saw no reason to expect lower rates ahead.
Lower German rates would have hurt the mark by reducing the relative value of assets priced in marks and the German unit kept rising after the Bundesbank announced its decision.
"The deutschemark should continue to strengthen, since now they don't expect a rate cut in Germany," said Dori Schwartz, associate international economist at Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette.
The dollar fell to 1.5175/80 marks from 1.5220/25 at the open, but edged higher to 112.81/91 yen from 112.72/77.
Perhaps the most dramatic recent move in currency markets has been the mark rally to 74.36 yen, its highest point in 44 months.
Japanese investors have poured money into overseas markets, notably Germany, in an effort to capture higher returns than those offered by meager-yielding Japanese securities, analysts said.
As a result, the mark has risen sharply against the yen, dollar and other European currencies, traders said.

"We're seeing overall mark strength. There is still a lot of disinvestment coming out of Japan into Europe, apparently into the mark first," said James Powers, corporate foreign exchange vice president at Westdeutsche Landesank Girozentrale in New York.
Meanwhile, the dollar spent most of the session parked just below 113 yen, bolstered by the yen's relative weakness against the mark.
Late in New York trading the dollar fell below 1.52 marks after holding near that level for most of the day.

Traders had cited solid buying interest from U.S. corporations and possibly European central banks for stabilizing the dollar at 1.52 marks. When that support gave way, speculators quickly pushed the dollar to 1.5160 marks, its low for the day.
"There doesn't seem to be tremendous interest in buying dollars, it's more buying and selling marks," said Jeffrey Yu, senior currency dealer at Sanwa Bank in New York.
Traders noted the dollar generally stayed in very narrow ranges Thursday after highly volatile trading in recent sessions.
Should the greenback make a serious move either higher toward the recent 33-month high at 113.12 yen or below key support at 1.5150 marks, heavy follow-up movement will likely ensue, dealers said.
"If the dollar goes either way, you're probably going to see some heavy action," Powers said.

Elsewhere, sterling rose to $1.5940/50 from $1.5915/25. The dollar slipped to 1.2550/60 Swiss francs from 1.2560/70. The greenback rose to Canadian $1.3455/60 from C$1.3441/46. The Australian dollar dipped to $0.7920/25 from $0.7921/26.
--Chris Stetkiewicz, 212-859-1664
